reviews.review:
I play a lot of physical pinball in real life. I don't expect the developer of a $5 pinball game on Steam to be Keith Elwin. That said, I was pretty disappointed by this game.

The playfields are mostly empty. There are no shots to make, really. Everything on the playfield is functionally a pop bumper, drop target, or spinner. In practice, this means each level has the same strategy: Up Top All Day, and after the 15th level or so it gets pretty samey to flip once or twice and watch the ball bounce between pops for a long time. 

The pinball itself has beach ball physics, and cradling it on a flipper and then releasing weirdly bounces it up into the air instead of nicely rolling down the flipper. Backhanding a shot in most circumstances is out of the question. The ball save shoots the pinball up between the flippers from the drain Bally Spectrum-style, and sometimes robs you.

The game would feel a lot more polished with some extra features. An online leaderboard, or camera options, or colorblindness settings would all be very welcome to make the experience feel more whole.

I wonder if the developer plays much pinball. The design language that you learn as a player just isn't here. Rampless pinball tables from the 60s and 70s found novel ways to make each table experience similar, but still unique and fun. Take inspiration from that deep well of ideas!
